verbalization: Decitabine is implicated in the pathogenesis of Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) through its role in inducing therapy-related AML and AML with specific chromosomal abnormalities. The evidence suggests that Decitabine, through its indication for Therapy-Related AML and Myelodysplastic Syndrome, is linked to Glasdegib, which in turn is associated with AML with the specific chromosomal abnormality Inv3(p21;q26.2) or T(3;3)(p21;q26.2). This connection is supported by the shared pathway involving Glasdegib, which is a known inhibitor of DNA methyltransferases and has been shown to affect the epigenetic regulation of genes involved in AML progression. The recurring involvement of Glasdegib in multiple pathways involving AML with distinct chromosomal abnormalities indicates a potential mechanism by which Decitabine may influence the development of this leukemia subtype. The evidence suggests that Decitabine may act through a mechanism involving Glasdegib, potentially by modulating epigenetic pathways, to contribute to the development of AML with the specified chromosomal abnormalities.
